A traffic signal cycles from GREEN to YELLOW, YELLOW to RED and RED to GREEN.
In each cycle, GREEN is turned on for 70 seconds, YELLOW is turned on for
5 seconds and the RED is turned on for 75 seconds. This traffic light has to be implemented
using a finite state machine (FSM). The only input to this FSM is a clock of 5 second period.
The minimum number of flip-flops required to implement this FSM is _______.
en.explanation:
According to the question,

Green is turned ON for 70 seconds

Yellow is turned ON for 5 seconds.

Red is turned ON for 75 seconds

$$ \therefore $$ Total time to complete one cycle for all 3 lights = (70 + 5 +75) seconds = 150 seconds

Available time period of clock = 5 seconds

Total number of clock cycles in one complete cycle = $${{150} \over 5}$$ = 30

Assume number of flip-flops required = n

We know possible number of states using n flip-flops = $${2^n}$$

So to get 30 clock cycle or 30 states,

$${2^n}$$ $$ \ge $$ 30

$$ \Rightarrow $$ n $$ \ge $$ 4.90

$$ \therefore $$ Minimum number of required flip-flops is = 5

A function F(A, B, C) defined by three Boolean variables A, B and C when expressed as sum of products is given by

F = $$\overline A .\overline B .\overline C + \overline A .B.\overline C + A.\overline B .\overline C $$

where, $$\overline A $$, $$\overline B $$, and $$\overline C $$ are the complements of the respective variables. The product of sums (POS) form of the function F is

options.content: F = (A + B + C)(A + $$\overline B $$ + C)($$\overline A $$ + B + C)
F = ($$\overline A $$ + $$\overline B $$ + $$\overline C $$)($$\overline A $$ + B + $$\overline C $$)(A + $$\overline B $$ + $$\overline C $$)

F = (A + B + $$\overline C $$)(A + $$\overline B $$ + $$\overline C $$)($$\overline A $$ + B + $$\overline C $$)($$\overline A $$ + $$\overline B $$ + C)($$\overline A $$ + $$\overline B $$ + $$\overline C $$)
F = ($$\overline A $$ + $$\overline B $$ + C)($$\overline A $$ + B + C)(A + $$\overline B $$ + C)(A + B + $$\overline C $$)(A + B + C)

en.explanation:
Given that :

F(A, B, C) = $$\overline A .\overline B .\overline C + \overline A .B.\overline C + A.\overline B .\overline C $$

$$\overline A .\overline B .\overline C$$ = 000 = 0

$$\overline A .B.\overline C$$ = 010 = 2

$$A.\overline B .\overline C $$ = 100 = 4

So, F(A, B, C) = $$\sum {\left( {0,2,4} \right)} $$

Above expression is in SOP form.

$$ \therefore $$ POS form is

F(A, B, C) = $$\pi \left( {1,3,5,6,7} \right)$$

                  = $$\pi \left( {001,011,101,110,111} \right)$$

In POS form,

001 = (A + B + $$\overline C $$)
011 = (A + $$\overline B $$ + $$\overline C $$)
101 = ($$\overline A $$ + B + $$\overline C $$)
110 = ($$\overline A $$ + $$\overline B $$ + C)
111 = ($$\overline A $$ + $$\overline B $$ + $$\overline C $$)

$$ \therefore $$ F(A, B, C) in POS form

= (A + B + $$\overline C $$)(A + $$\overline B $$ + $$\overline C $$)($$\overline A $$ + B + $$\overline C $$)($$\overline A $$ + $$\overline B $$ + C)($$\overline A $$ + $$\overline B $$ + $$\overline C $$)

Consider matrix $$A = \left[ {\matrix{ k & {2k} \cr {{k^2} - k} & {{k^2}} \cr } } \right]$$ and

vector $$X = \left[ {\matrix{ {{x_1}} \cr {{x_2}} \cr } } \right]$$.

The number of distinct real values of k for which the equation AX = 0 has infinitely many solutions is _______.
en.explanation:
Given that,

$$A = \left[ {\matrix{ k & {2k} \cr {{k^2} - k} & {{k^2}} \cr } } \right]$$ and $$X = \left[ {\matrix{ {{x_1}} \cr {{x_2}} \cr } } \right]$$

and AX = 0

Which means it is in the form of Homogenous equation.

According to the question,

the system must have infinitely many solutions.

Which is possible only when

|A| = 0

$$ \Rightarrow $$ $$\left| {\matrix{ k & {2k} \cr {{k^2} - k} & {{k^2}} \cr } } \right|$$ = 0

$$ \Rightarrow $$ k3 - 2k(k2 - k) = 0

$$ \Rightarrow $$ k3 - 2k3 + 2k2 = 0

$$ \Rightarrow $$ 2k2 - k3 = 0

$$ \Rightarrow $$ k2(2 - k) = 0

$$ \Rightarrow $$ k = 0, 2

$$ \therefore $$ Number of distinct values of K for infinite number of solutions = 2.

Consider the network shown below with R1 = 1 $$\Omega $$, R2 = 2 $$\Omega $$ and R3 = 3 $$\Omega $$. The network is connected to a constant voltage source of 11 V.

The magnitude of the current (in amperes, accurate to two decimal places) through the source is _______.
en.explanation:
Given R1 = 1 $$\Omega$$, R2 = 2 $$\Omega$$, R3 = 3 $$\Omega$$

Network is symmetric; so VA = VB and VC = VD.

So the circuits reduces to

$${R_{eq}} = ({R_1}||{R_1}) + ({R_1}||{R_1}||{R_3}||{R_3}) + ({R_1}||{R_1})$$

$${R_{eq}} = {{{R_1}} \over 2} + \left( {{{{R_1}} \over 2}||{{{R_3}} \over 2}} \right) + {{{R_1}} \over 2}$$

$$ = {R_1} + {{({R_1} \times {R_3})} \over {{{{R_1}} \over 2} + {{{R_3}} \over 2}}} = {R_1} + {{{R_1}{R_3}} \over {2({R_1} + {R_3})}}$$

$$ = 1 + {{1 \times 3} \over {2(1 + 3)}} = 1 + {3 \over 8} = {{11} \over 8}$$

$${I_s} = {{{V_s}} \over {{R_{eq}}}} = {{11} \over {11/8}} = 8A$$
